remazu.title: ReMazu: Iterations of Devotion 新妈祖崇拜
description: This project recalls snippets from the cyclical journeys of a deity named Mazu, a sea goddess and shaman who was first mythologized in Fujian in Southern China. An ancestral wanderer, she came to me initially in web searches, materializing in the form of a 3D model across a short film and 3D printed sculptures. Through research, writing, and prototyping, I reimagine Mazu with a third hand, a Daoist apparatus for wielding the craft of eros-technics.

Echoing the iterative nature of 3D modeling, the animation uses iterative calling to frame Mazu as an emotional reprogramming loop: the act of inviting her triggers the process of remothering. Iteration is in itself a form of devotion.

sibuxiang.title: Sibuxiang: The Four Not-Likes
sibuxiang.summary: The Four Not-Likes (四不象) is an interactive performance centered around a hybrid quadruped creature whose movement is controlled through a custom physical interface.
description: The Four Not-Likes (四不象) takes its name from the Chinese mythological creature Sibuxiang, whose body appears to contain features of multiple animals while belonging fully to none. The project centers around a digitally modeled and animated quadruped creature inhabiting a virtual environment.

Built through a pipeline spanning 3D modeling, character animation, game-engine development and physical hardware, the work connects the creature's movement in Unity to a custom arcade-style controller. Through this relationship between bodily input, virtual movement and the hybrid creature, the project explores different ways of inhabiting and navigating a digital body.

triadic-patterning.title: Triadic Patterning
triadic-patterning.summary: A Sequel to ReMazu: Iterations of Devotion
description: Triadic Patterning is a worldbuilding project that evolved across a three-channel video, interactive website, and 3D printed sculpture. It explores the triadic relationship between Qianliyan (Thousand-Mile Eye), Shunfeng’er (Wind-Following Ear), and Mazu. Qianliyan and Shunfeng’er are guardian deities embodying the act of seeing and listening, appearing in myth as anthropomorphic tools. In my reframing, Qianliyan and Shunfeng’er cause havoc due to their separation and unexamined pain; sensing this chaos, Mazu binds them together in a contract of Daoist magic, completing a triadic patterning of embodied integration.

grand-street.title: Grand Street
description: Grand St. (2018) is a camp-horror experimental film exploring the visceral experience of engaging with a familiar environment. Using sliding as both a literal movement and a experiential metaphor, the film wavers quickly between the surreal and the mundane; it is committed to depicting the vibrant, fertile, and sensorily-rich haunts of Manhattan New York's Chinatown.
exhibitions: Grand St. was shown at the Flat Earth Film Festival (2019), and as a part of PRACTICE X Wind (2018) at Artist’s Space.

a-tour-of-famous-landmarks.title: A Tour of Famous Landmarks
description: a live performance that uses machine-vision landmark detection to remap the body into an inner landscape, inspired by the Daoist diagram Nei Jing Tu. A webcam tracks my movement in real time and translates tapping gestures into “site activations” on a projected display.

lunar-calendar.title: Wing On Wo 2024 Lunar Calendar Design
description: Design for Wing On Wo's Fourth Edition of From Chinatown, With Love, a Lunar New Year Calendar that celebrates the Year of the Wood Dragon by featuring local businesses in Manhattan Chinatown.

amorous-polymers.title: Amorous Polymers enterprise
description: AmorousPolymers is a series of photoshoots that explore tenderness, abandonment, and erotic play, activated by 3D printed and hand-made body accessories.
